literature_notes: All seven ledger lines describe C-terminal fusions (1D4, Strep-II, FLAG, EGFP) appended after the last residue of either the truncated construct (hCALHM1Δct, residues 1–303) or the full-length protein (residues 1–346). Both termini fall within the large intracellular C-terminal domain (topology landmark: INTRACELLULAR 203–346), so none of these tags is on the extracellular face. L1 mentions Lys123 (ECL2, extracellular) as the site of NHS-SS-biotin labelling used to confirm surface trafficking of the 1D4-tagged construct; this is a chemical biotinylation probe, not an epitope-tag insertion, and does not qualify under the ledger rules. L3 lists seven point-mutant positions (Leu67, Ile109, Val112, Ala116, Thr196, Val192, Ala199) that are all within transmembrane helices (TM2: 51–71; TM3: 107–120; TM4: 182–202) and represent mutagenesis probes of the pore, not tag-insertion sites. No ledger line reports a tolerated epitope-tag, fluorescent-protein, or domain insertion at any extracellular position of CALHM1. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal 1D4 epitope tag appended after residue 303 of hCALHM1Δct; residue 303 (Leu) lies within the intracellular C-terminal domain (topology 203–346), so the tag faces the cytoplasm.
C-terminal EGFP (and FLAG in L5) fused after the last residue (Val346) of full-length CALHM1; residue 346 is within the intracellular C-terminal domain (topology 203–346).
